judged_text: In updateEvent the same dead fallback (`find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy) yields undefined for selectedCalendar where the old code used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Rescheduling a booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.update with an undefined calendarId, which fails; the booking's new time in the app silently drifts from the Google Calendar event that was never updated.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback for `selectedCalendar` in `updateEvent` is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the exact case this branch is meant to handle), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will almost always fail and yield `undefined`. Previously the fallback used `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` (single DC), which would have provided a calendar id. With destinationCalendar now an array, the analogous fallback should use the first/appropriate destination calendar, not a `find` keyed on a missing value. This can lead to `calendarId` being missing or defaulting incorrectly, causing updates to fail or hit the wrong calendar when a booking reference lacks `externalCalendarId` (a scenario visible in the codepaths that pass nullable `externalCalendarId`).
